blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Visuomotor policies trained through imitation learning are highly sensitive to changes in camera viewpoint. This is particularly problematic for mobile manipulation (MoMa), where robots rarely execute manipulation from the exact same base pose used during demonstration collection due to navigation uncertainty, localization drift, and environmental constraints. Recent approaches use novel-view synthesis (NVS) to augment demonstrations with unseen viewpoints, but they assume static scenes and therefore fail to re-render the manipulated object during the post-contact interaction phase, leaving the most critical parts of the demonstration unaugmented. We present MOMASPLAT, a novel-view demonstration augmentation framework for mobile manipulation that synthesizes full manipulation trajectories from unseen robot base poses, including dynamic object interactions. Our key insight is that standard MoMa data collection naturally provides the multiview observations needed to reconstruct both the static scene and the manipulated object in 3D. MOMASPLAT combines 3D Gaussian Splatting, feed-forward 3D foundation models, and kinematics-based action retargeting to separately reconstruct the scene and manipulated object, render them from novel viewpoints, and generate geometrically consistent synthetic demonstrations paired with transformed actions. We evaluate MOMASPLAT on five real-world mobile manipulation tasks involving both rigid and articulated objects across three scenes, and validate the fidelity of its synthesized demonstrations against ground truth in simulation. MOMASPLAT substantially improves robustness to unseen base poses, more than doubling the average success rate of the strongest baseline and maintaining non-trivial success at large base displacements where all baselines fail, while reducing the need for largescale real-world data collection.
blocks.zh: 通过模仿学习培训的维苏莫托尔政策对镜头视角的变化高度敏感. 这对于移动操控(MoMa)来说尤其成问题,因为由于导航不确定性,本地化漂移,以及环境限制,机器人很少从演示采集时所用的完全相同的基位进行操控. 近代方法使用新视觉合成(NVS)来用看不见的观点来增强演示,但是它们假设的是静态场景,因此在接触后互动阶段未能重新让出被操纵的物体,使得演示中最关键的部分没有被提升. 我们提出MOMASPLAT,是一种用于移动操纵的新视角演示增强框架,它从看不见的机器人基面合成了全部操纵轨迹,包括动态物体相互作用. 我们的关键见解是,标准的MOMA数据收集自然提供了重建静态场景和3D中被操纵物体所需的多视图观测. MOMASPLAT结合了3D高斯白板,向导3D基础模型,以及基于动能的动作重定向,分别重建场景和被操纵的物体,从新颖的观点使其形成,并生成几何一致的合成演示与变形动作配对. 我们评价MOMASPLAT在五个现实世界的移动操纵任务,这些任务涉及三个场景的刚性物体和清晰的物体,并验证其在模拟中针对地面真理的综合演示的忠实性。 MOMASPLAT大大改进了坚固度,使其达到不为人知的基数,使最强基线的平均成功率翻了一番以上,并在所有基准都失效的大型基数迁移中保持非三边成功,同时减少大规模实际世界数据收集的需要。

blocks.en: I INTRODUCTION
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en:
Imitation learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for training visuomotor policies that perform complex manipulation tasks directly from image observations [ 1 , 2 ] .
However, these policies are notoriously sensitive to changes in camera viewpoint [ 3 , 4 , 5 ] .
Even small deviations in camera pose can significantly degrade performance, since the policy learns a narrow visual distribution tied to the demonstrations used during training.
blocks.zh:
模仿学习已成为一种强有力的范例,用于培训直接从图像观测中执行复杂操纵任务的机动人员政策[1,2]。
然而,这些政策对镜头视角的变化极为敏感[3、4、5]。
即使是相机外形的微小偏差也会显著地降低性能,因为政策学习了与训练中使用的演示相关的狭义视觉分布.

blocks.en:
This sensitivity is particularly problematic for mobile manipulation (MoMa).
Unlike tabletop manipulation setups, where demonstrations are often collected from a fixed robot camera pose, mobile manipulators rarely execute tasks from the exact same location at deployment time.
Navigation uncertainty, localization drift, obstacle avoidance, and imperfect planning routinely place the robot at different base poses relative to the workspace.
As a result, the robot observes the manipulation scene from viewpoints that may differ substantially from those seen during demonstration collection.
Robust deployment therefore requires visuomotor policies that generalize across a distribution of robot base poses rather than a single viewpoint.
blocks.zh:
这种灵敏度对于移动操纵(MoMa)特别有问题.
与平板电脑操纵设置不同,通常从固定机器人相机姿势中收集演示材料,移动操纵器在部署时很少从完全相同的地点执行任务.
导航不确定性、本地化漂移、避免障碍和不完善的规划通常将机器人置于与工作空间不同的基部。
因此,机器人从可能与示范收集过程中所看到的观点大相径庭的角度观察操纵场景.
因此,强有力的部署需要机动化政策,将机器人基地的分布普遍化,而不是单一的观点。

blocks.en:
A straightforward solution would be to collect demonstrations from many different robot locations.
However, large-scale real-world teleoperation is expensive and difficult to scale [ 6 , 2 , 7 ] .
Recent work has therefore explored synthesizing additional demonstrations through novel-view synthesis (NVS), generating virtual observations from unseen viewpoints using real-world captures [ 8 , 9 , 10 ] .
While promising, existing approaches assume a static scene and therefore fail during the most important part of manipulation: object interaction.
Since the manipulated object moves throughout the demonstration, prior NVS methods cannot consistently re-render the object from novel viewpoints during the post-contact interaction phase, restricting augmentation primarily to pre-contact motions or introducing geometrically inconsistent generations.
blocks.zh:
一个直接的解决办法是从许多不同的机器人地点收集演示。
然而,大规模现实世界电信业务费用昂贵,难以扩大[6,2,7].
因此,最近的工作探索了通过小说-观点综合(NVS)合成更多的演示,利用现实世界的捕捉[8,9,10]从看不见的观点产生虚拟观测.
现有方法虽然很有希望,但有一个静态场景,因此在操纵的最重要部分 -- -- 物体相互作用 -- -- 中失败。
由于被操纵对象在整个演示过程中移动,先前的NVS方法无法在接触后互动阶段从新观点中一致地将对象重放,将增强主要限制在接触前运动或引入几何不一致的代相.

blocks.en:
In this work, we present MoMaSplat , a demonstration augmentation framework for mobile manipulation that synthesizes complete manipulation trajectories from unseen robot base poses, including dynamic object interactions (Fig. 1 ).
Our key insight is that standard mobile-manipulation data collection naturally provides the multi-view observations needed to reconstruct both the static scene and the manipulated object in 3D.
During navigation, the robot observes the scene from diverse viewpoints that enable scene reconstruction, while the manipulation demonstrations themselves provide object-centric observations that enable reconstructing the manipulated object and its motion.
blocks.zh:
在这部作品中,我们介绍了MoMaSplat ,这是移动操纵的演示增强框架,它从看不见的机器人基面上合成了完整的操纵轨迹,包括动态物体相互作用(图1).
我们的关键见解是,标准的移动操纵数据收集自然提供了重建静态场景和被操纵的3D物体所需的多视图观测.
在导航期间,机器人从多种观点观察场景,这些观点使得场景重建成为可能,而操控演示本身则提供以物体为中心的观测,使被操控的物体得以重建并进行运动.

blocks.en:
Building on this observation, MoMaSplat separately reconstructs the static scene and manipulated objects using 3D Gaussian Splatting [ 11 ] and feed-forward 3D foundation models [ 12 ] .
Given a novel robot base pose, MoMaSplat re-renders the scene, manipulated object, and robot from the new viewpoint and retargets the original actions through kinematics-based transformations to generate geometrically consistent synthetic demonstrations.
blocks.zh:
基于这一观察,MoMaSplatz分别重建了静态场景并使用3D高斯平板电脑[11]和feed-forward 3D基础模型[12]被操纵的物体.
由于有新颖的机器人基础姿势,MoMaSplatz从新角度将场景,被操纵的物体和机器人重现出场面,并通过以动能为基础的转换来重新瞄准原作,以产生几何一致的合成演示.

blocks.en:
We evaluate MoMaSplat on five real-world mobile manipulation tasks involving both rigid and articulated objects across three scenes, and validate the fidelity of its synthesized demonstrations against ground truth in simulation.
Our experiments show that MoMaSplat substantially improves robustness to unseen deployment-time base poses, outperforming prior augmentation approaches across 12 12 unseen base poses ( 3 3 rollouts per pose) per task as the robot moves farther away from the source demonstration locations.
blocks.zh:
我们评价MoMaSplat的五个真实世界移动操纵任务,这些任务涉及三个场景的僵硬和清晰的物体,并验证其在模拟中针对地面真理的综合演示的忠实性。
我们的实验显示,MoMaSplat大大改进了坚固度,以至隐蔽部署时间基座,在12个隐蔽基座上表现优于先前的增强方法(每个站位3个站台),随着机器人远离源头演示地点。

blocks.en: Our contributions are threefold: • A novel-view demonstration augmentation framework for mobile manipulation that synthesizes complete trajectories, including dynamic object interactions. • A geometry-consistent generation pipeline that separately reconstructs scenes and manipulated objects and retargets actions to unseen base poses. • Substantial improvements in robustness to deployment-time viewpoint variation across multiple real-world mobile manipulation tasks.
blocks.zh: 我们的贡献有三个方面: • 移动操纵的新视角演示增强框架,它综合了完整的轨迹,包括动态物体相互作用. 二. 支助 一个几何-相容的生成管道,它分别重建场景和被操纵的物体并重新将动作瞄准隐形基站. • 在部署时间角度的稳健性方面大有改进,因为现实世界的移动操纵任务各不相同。

blocks.en: II Related Work
blocks.zh: 二. 相关工作

blocks.en:
Our method proposes a solution to train imitation learning visuomotor policies for mobile manipulators via data augmentation.
Here, we review the most relevant related work in those areas.
blocks.zh:
我们的方法提出了一个解决方案,通过数据扩增,为移动操纵者培训模拟学习方法。
在这方面,我们审查这些领域最相关的工作。

blocks.en: Demonstration Synthesis in Simulation. A prominent line of work synthesizes new demonstrations by replaying source actions in randomized simulated scenes. The X-Gen family [ 7 , 13 , 14 , 15 , 16 ] procedurally generates data by transforming and sequencing object-centric trajectory segments, with extensions such as MoMaGen [ 15 ] addressing mobile-manipulation constraints like base reachability and visibility. However, because the generated plans are purely kinematic, they typically rely on open-loop on-robot rollouts to verify feasibility and capture visual observations, at a cost that rivals manual data collection [ 17 , 8 ] . A parallel line of work uses simulators to generate data from multiple viewpoints [ 18 , 19 , 20 ] , but requires modeling the full environment and task dynamics in simulation, suffering from the visual and physical sim-to-real gap. Our work avoids on-robot rollouts and full-scene simulation by reconstructing the real scene and manipulated object via novel-view synthesis, using simulation only to render the known robot embodiment.
blocks.zh: 模拟中演示合成. 突出一行的工作通过在随机模拟场景中重放源动作来合成新的演示. X-Gen家族[7,13,14,15,16]在程序上通过改变和排序以物体为中心轨迹段来生成数据,其扩展如MoMaGen[15]解决了可达到性和能见度等移动操纵限制. 然而,由于所生成的计划纯粹是动能的,因此它们通常依靠开放-loop on-robot推出来验证可行性并捕捉可视观测,成本与人工数据收集相竞争[17,8]. 一个平行的工作线使用模拟器从多角度生成数据[18,19,20],但需要在模拟中建模完整的环境和任务动态,受视觉和物理的模拟-现实差距之苦. 我们的工作通过重建真实的场景和通过小说取景合成被操纵的对象,避免了机器人上出场和全场模拟,只利用模拟来使已知的机器人化身.

blocks.en: Demonstration Augmentation from Real-World Captures. Beyond 2D image augmentation [ 21 , 22 , 23 ] , recent methods synthesize observations from real-world captures. Neural simulators [ 24 , 25 , 26 ] use generative video models but can suffer from hallucinations and geometric inconsistencies. Alternatively, novel-view synthesis (NVS) enables viewpoint augmentation [ 9 , 10 , 17 , 27 , 28 , 29 , 30 , 31 ] . VISTA [ 27 ] uses ZeroNVS [ 32 ] , while Yang et al. [ 9 ] employ 3D Gaussian Splatting [ 11 ] ; however, both focus on third-person tabletop settings requiring multi-camera pre-scans. Closer to our setting, One-Thousand Trajectories [ 8 ] supports moving eye-in-hand cameras, while EgoDemoGen [ 33 ] generates paired egocentric observations and actions using a generative model. However, these methods do not explicitly reconstruct dynamic objects and restrict augmentation to pre-contact motion. In contrast, MoMaSplat jointly models the static scene and manipulated objects, enabling kinematically consistent augmentation across both pre-contact and post-contact interaction phases for mobile robots with egocentric cameras.

blocks.en: Mobile Manipulation. Mobile manipulation remains a key challenge in robot learning [ 34 , 35 , 36 , 37 , 38 ] , particularly in selecting robot base poses. Traditional methods use geometric heuristics such as Inverse Reachability Maps [ 39 , 40 , 41 ] , while learning-based navigation [ 42 , 43 , 44 , 45 ] often overlooks downstream policy sensitivity to viewpoint changes. Mobi- π \pi [ 3 ] selects base poses matching the training distribution but requires pre-scanning and test-time optimization. In contrast, we train policies robust to diverse base poses, reducing the need for precise base placement at deployment.

blocks.en: III MoMaSplat
blocks.zh: 三 摩马斯平板

blocks.en: We aim to augment a mobile-manipulation dataset with synthetic demonstrations from unseen robot base poses. From source demonstrations at a few robot locations, MoMaSplat synthesizes observations and actions for nearby deployment-time poses never physically demonstrated.
blocks.zh: 我们的目标是用来自看不见的机器人基地的合成演示来增强移动操纵数据集。 MoMaSplat从几个机器人地点的源头演示中,综合了附近部署时间的观察和行动,从未实际展示。

blocks.en:
To achieve this, MoMaSplat decomposes the environment into three components: i) a static scene model, ii) a dynamic object model for the manipulated object, and iii) the robot embodiment itself.
The scene and object models are reconstructed independently and aligned into a shared metric frame.
A key observation is that the navigation trajectories naturally provide the bridge between both reconstructions: during navigation, the manipulated objects remain static, allowing the object-centric and scene-centric trajectories to be consistently registered.
blocks.zh:
为了实现这一点,MoMaSplate将环境分解为三个部分:一)静态场景模型;二)被被操纵物体的动态物体模型;和三)机器人化身本身.
场景和物体模型独立地被重建,并被调整为一个共享的度量框.
一个关键观察是,导航轨迹自然地提供了两个重建之间的桥梁:在导航期间被操纵的物体保持静止状态,使得以物体为中心,以场景为中心的轨迹能够始终如一地被登记.

blocks.en: For augmentation, given a sampled robot base pose, MoMaSplat renders the scene, manipulated object, and robot from the corresponding viewpoint and retargets the demonstrated actions through kinematic transformations. The resulting observations and transformed actions form synthetic demonstrations that augment the dataset for policy training. Fig. 2 provides an overview of the full process.
blocks.zh: 对于增强,由于一个被取样的机器人基础姿势,MoMaSplat使场景,被操纵的物体,以及机器人从相应角度出发,通过动能转换重新瞄准所显示的行动. 由此产生的观测结果和转变后的行动构成合成演示,为政策培训增加了数据集。 图2概述了整个过程。

Paired with the transformed actions a ~ 1 : L j \tilde{a}_{1:L_{j}} , this forms a synthetic demonstration; repeating across sampled poses yields the generated dataset. Problem Formulation. We consider an imitation learning setting on a mobile manipulator operating in a scene.
The robot alternates between two modes of operation: navigation, which changes the robot base pose, and manipulation, which executes arm actions from a fixed base location.
We represent the robot base pose as a transform T w b ∈ S ​ E ​ ( 2 ) {}^{b}_{w}T\in SE(2) with respect to a stationary world frame w w , parameterized by a planar position ( x b , y b ) (x_{b},y_{b}) and heading θ b \theta_{b} .
The robot observes the scene through an egocentric RGB camera mounted on the robot body (e.g., head or torso).
The camera pose relative to the robot base is determined by the robot configuration through forward kinematics, such that both changes in base pose and articulation of the robot body induce changes in viewpoint.

Our goal is to augment the source manipulation dataset 𝒟 src \mathcal{D}_{\text{src}} with a synthetic dataset 𝒟 gen \mathcal{D}_{\text{gen}} of demonstrations generated at unseen base poses
to obtain a base-pose robust policy trained on 𝒟 = 𝒟 src ∪ 𝒟 gen \mathcal{D}=\mathcal{D}_{\text{src}}\cup\mathcal{D}_{\text{gen}} . To achieve this, MoMaSplat first reconstructs the scene and manipulated objects in 3D and aligns them into a shared metric frame (Sec. III-A ). It then synthesizes demonstrations from sampled base poses by rendering the scene, object, and robot from the corresponding viewpoint and retargeting the actions and proprioception to remain geometrically consistent (Sec. III-B ). The synthesized demonstrations are combined with the source dataset for policy training (Sec. III-C ).

blocks.en: III-A 3D Reconstruction
blocks.zh: 三. A 3D 重建

blocks.en:
To synthesize demonstrations from unseen robot base poses, MoMaSplat requires a 3D representation that can be rendered from arbitrary viewpoints. A central challenge is that manipulation involves dynamic objects whose pose changes throughout the demonstration. Unlike prior novel-view synthesis approaches that model the environment as a single static scene, MoMaSplat reconstructs the static scene and manipulated objects separately, leveraging observations naturally produced during mobile-manipulation data collection. Navigation
trajectories cover the environment while the objects are static, and manipulation trajectories
capture the objects in motion.

blocks.en: 3D Scene Model Reconstruction. As the robot moves through the workspace, its camera naturally captures diverse viewpoints, providing the multi-view coverage needed for 3D reconstruction without external cameras or scanning. We therefore use 𝒟 nav \mathcal{D}_{\text{nav}} to build a photorealistic 3D scene model: we recover per-image camera poses with structure-from-motion via COLMAP [ 46 ] , which also produces a sparse point cloud that initializes a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) [ 11 ] reconstruction.
blocks.zh: 三维 场景模型重建. 当机器人穿过工作空间时,其相机自然能捕捉到不同的观点,提供3D重建所需的多视图覆盖,而无需外部相机或扫描. 因此,我们使用 D nav \ mathcal{ D}_{\text{ nav}}} 来构建一个相片现实化的 三维场景模型: 我们通过 COLMAP [46] 恢复由结构起动的 per-image相机的相机,它也产生出一个稀有的点云来初始化了 三维高斯平板 (3DGS) [11] 重建.

blocks.en: We optimize the Gaussians by minimizing a photometric loss between rendered and observed images. Since the scene is not perfectly static across navigation trajectories, transient content may appear between demonstrations; we adopt the uncertainty-aware formulation of WildGaussians [ 47 ] , which down-weights inconsistent regions during optimization to yield a robust model 𝒢 scene \mathcal{G}_{\text{scene}} . We additionally mask out pixels belonging to the manipulated object and the robot during scene reconstruction, preventing the object from being baked into 𝒢 scene \mathcal{G}_{\text{scene}} and avoiding a static “ghost” when the independently reconstructed dynamic object is later composited into the scene.

blocks.en: Structure-from-motion reconstructs the scene only up to an unknown global scale, while our framework transforms metric actions and therefore requires a metric reconstruction. We recover the scale using the robot’s onboard depth sensor: for the frames in 𝒟 nav \mathcal{D}_{\text{nav}} , we compare the measured depth maps to depth maps rendered from 𝒢 scene \mathcal{G}_{\text{scene}} and take the median per-pixel ratio of measured to rendered depth as the scale factor.

blocks.en:
3D Object Model Reconstruction. Since the object of interest moves independently from the scene, we build a separate 3DGS model for it.
Conceptually, the steps mirror those for the scene: we estimate the object’s pose in each frame and use these poses to optimize a 3D Gaussian reconstruction.
However, the challenges here are different.
Correspondence-based methods [ 46 ] are poorly suited to small, weakly-textured objects,
while instance-level pose trackers [ 48 ] require an existing 3D model of the object, which is not available to us. Instead, we find that our setting is amenable to recent feed-forward 3D foundation models, like VGGT [ 49 , 12 ] , which estimate camera poses directly from an unposed RGB sequence.

blocks.en: III-B Synthesizing Demonstrations from Unseen Base Poses
blocks.zh: 三-B 由不明基地可能性合成演示

blocks.en:
Given the scene and object models, our framework synthesizes new demonstrations at unseen base poses in three stages. For each original robot base pose, T i w b {}^{\mathit{b}}_{\mathit{w}}{T}_{i} , we first sample a set of target base poses that cover possible deployment-time locations while remaining kinematically feasible (e.g., reachable for the arm).
We then synthesize each source demonstration from each sampled pose by composing three separately rendered streams: the static scene (from the 3D scene model), the manipulated objects (from the 3D object model), and the robot body as seen from the new base location.
Finally, we retarget the source action to be defined with respect to the virtual sampled base location to obtain a new pair of virtual image and action label.

鉴于场景和物体模型,我们的框架将隐形基地的新演示合成三个阶段。 对于每个原始的机器人基础姿势,Ti w b {}^{\mathit{b}}_{\mathit{w}}{T}_{i},我们首先对一组目标基础姿势进行取样,以覆盖可能的部署时间位置,同时保持运动上的可行性(例如,手臂可以到达).
然后,我们通过编组三个独立渲染的流来从每个被取样的姿势中合成每个源演示:静态场景(出自3D场景模型),被操纵的物体(出自3D物体模型),从新的基座位置看到的机器人体.
最后,我们重新确定要针对虚拟取样基址定义的源行动,以获得一对新的虚拟图像和动作标签。

blocks.zh: 四. 实验评价

blocks.en:
We evaluate MoMaSplat on five real-world mobile manipulation tasks across three scenes, comparing against four baselines: no augmentation and three augmentation methods. Our experiments focus on a) whether MoMaSplat improves policy success at unseen base poses, b) how performance varies with the distance between the deployment-time base pose and the closest demonstration pose, and c) how policy success changes with the number of source demonstrations available for augmentation. Additionally, we evaluate the quality
of the generated data itself. This requires ground truth observations at poses where no
demonstration was collected, which is impractical in the real world. A human
teleoperator produces a different motion on every attempt, so even a re-collected
trajectory cannot serve as ground-truth for the generated demonstration.
Therefore, we develop one task in simulation , where camera and object poses are
known and source trajectories can be replayed from arbitrary base poses.

blocks.en: IV-B Results
blocks.zh: 四-B 结果

blocks.en:
Performance at Unseen Base Poses. Our main experimental results for policy success using MoMaSplat are summarized in
Fig. 4 , where success rates are binned by their minimum distance to the nearest demonstration pose. We additionally evaluate the 3 original demonstration base poses with 15 rollouts per pose. At the original base poses, all methods perform comparably. The picture changes sharply at unseen poses. When we average the results over all five tasks, MoMaSplat succeeds on 37% of unseen evaluations, more than twice the rate of the strongest baseline ( One-Thousand Trajectories at 17%) and four to six times that of the remaining baselines ( Source Only 6%, VISTA 8%, Action Augmentation 6%). Critically, Source Only and Action Augmentation collapse to near-zero success beyond 10 cm on most tasks, confirming that perturbing actions without changing the observation gives little robustness to base-pose shifts. VISTA performs poorly throughout; since it is designed for static-base settings, it does not transform actions to match the synthesized viewpoints. Moreover, its lack of temporal consistency produces jittery camera trajectories that further degrade the augmented data. One-Thousand Trajectories degrades more gracefully but still falls off at large distances, since it augments only the free-space approach motion. MoMaSplat achieves the highest overall unseen-pose success rate on every task, outperforming or matching all baselines across every unseen distance bin while sustaining substantial performance at the largest evaluated distances. For example, MoMaSplat achieves 33% on Pick-Place Bottle at 30 cm and 50% on Close Laptop at 40 cm, where every baseline has dropped to zero success rates.

blocks.en: Effect of Number of Source Demonstrations. To evaluate how the number of source demonstrations affects MoMaSplat , we use the Pick-Place Bottle task and train policies using 10, 50, and 90 source demonstrations. For each source demonstration, we generate 10 synthetic demonstrations. Across four test locations at a distance of 10 10 – 20 20 cm from the demonstration poses, we observe that success degrades gracefully with fewer source demonstrations. Specifically, we achieve success rates of 33 % 33\% , 42 % 42\% , and 50 % 50\% for 10, 50, and 90 source demonstrations, respectively. For reference, training on the full set of 90 source demonstrations without augmentation yields only an 8 % 8\% success rate at the same test poses. These results show that MoMaSplat substantially improves base-pose robustness even with a limited number of source demonstrations.

blocks.en: V Conclusion and Limitations
blocks.zh: 五. 结论和限制

blocks.en: Conclusion. We propose MoMaSplat , a framework for novel-view augmentation of mobile manipulation demonstrations that reconstructs the static scene and manipulated object in 3D, then re-renders full demonstrations, including the post-contact interaction phase, from unseen base poses. Unlike prior NVS augmentation methods that model only the static scene, MoMaSplat produces geometrically consistent observations across the entire trajectory. Across five real-world tasks in three scenes, this improves policy robustness, outperforming prior augmentation methods and maintaining performance beyond the distances where baselines fail. We will publicly release our code to support further research.
blocks.zh: 结论。 我们提议MoMaSplat(MoMaSplatz)为移动操纵演示提供新视觉增强框架, 与以往仅模拟静态场景的NVS扩能方法不同,MoMaSplatz在整个轨迹中产生几何一致的观测. 在三个场景中,在现实世界的五个任务中,这提高了政策稳健性,超过了先前的增强方法,使业绩维持在基线失效的距离之外。 我们将公开发布我们的代码以支持进一步的研究。

blocks.en: Limitations. MoMaSplat assumes mostly static scenes and rigid, visible objects, making deformable objects, heavy occlusions, and texture-poor surfaces challenging. Furthermore, because 𝒢 scene \mathcal{G}_{\text{scene}} is reconstructed from pre-interaction navigation views with object masks excluded, regions occluded by the object in its initial state (such as the surface beneath a lifted bottle or the interior of an opened drawer or air-fryer basket) are never observed during scene reconstruction and remain unmodeled when disoccluded. It also depends on consistent open-world segmentation and produces non-physical demonstrations by replaying source object trajectories without modeling contact forces or dynamics. Finally, view quality depends on navigation-data coverage. Addressing dynamic backgrounds, deformable objects, physical contact, and cluttered scenes remains future work.
blocks.zh: 限制。 MoMaSplat假设大部分是静态场景和刚性,可见的物体,使得可变形的物体,重的隐蔽物,以及质地贫瘠的表面具有挑战性. 此外,由于 G scene { mathcal{G}_{\text{ scene} 是从排除对象口罩的交互导航前视图重建而来,因此物体在其初始状态下所占据的区域(如被抬起的瓶子下方的地表或打开的抽屉或空管篮子的内部)在场景重建期间从未被观察到,被忽略时仍没有被模型化. 它还依赖于一致的开放-世界分化,并通过在不建模接触力或动态的情况下重放源物体轨迹来产生非物理的演示. 最后,取景质量取决于导航数据覆盖. 处理动态背景、可变形物体、物理接触和杂乱的场景仍然是今后的工作。
